newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee tracks weak NY, slips from peaks.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee tracks weak NY, slips from peaks.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures, tracking early losses on nearby New York contracts, ended Thursday with pared gains.
September, London's benchmark, slipped from its highs of $1,617 per tonne to end the day $18 up at $1,578 and well below the psychologically-important $1,600 mark.
"It was quite a disappointing day in coffee," said one trader. "It's mainly tracking New York, not up as much and not down as much."
Origin selling and price-fixing from Africa and Indonesia capped the gains.
The day's volume of 4,484 lots was boosted by active Sept/Nov switches as players rolled forward their position ahead of July's expiry next week.
Looking forward, traders said the robusta futures were likely to consolidate around current levels after Tuesday's sell-off which took September to six-month lows of $1,477.
"I think it won't come off too much. There are quite strong buyers below these levels," one said.
New York's September retraced to post a loss of six cents a lb at midday after failing to clear Wednesday's peak of 184.50 cents.
"It's formed a double top now. People were getting out by selling Sept/Dec switches," the trader said.

New York's arabica futures jumped sharply for the second day in a row on Wednesday as speculators continued to buy heavily in anticipation of a shortage of exchange-certified coffee for delivery against September.
That buying now seemed to have been overdone, some traders said.
Robustas need to break out of its tightening $1,545-$1,610 band basis September before attempting further upside move.
"We have seen a bottom. But until we get above $1,700, we can't talk of a bullish move yet," another said.
